harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, created a filesystem-enforced 100MB quota for datauser under /srv/data using an XFS loopback filesystem (since the root disk is a single XFS partition with no separate /srv mount, and XFS project/user quotas cannot be added via remount). Created user datauser, formatted a 300MB backing image, mounted it at /srv/data with usrquota, persisted it in /etc/fstab, and set bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser via xfs_quota. Verified enforcement (write stopped exactly at 100MB with "Disk quota exceeded"), then restarted node1 (systemctl reboot), confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified the mount, quota configuration, and enforcement all persisted and worked correctly after reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 filesystem layout, OS (RHEL 10), and confirmed root is a single XFS partition with no dedicated /srv mount
Created user datauser
Created 300MB backing image /var/lib/quota-images/srv-data.img, formatted as XFS
Mounted image at /srv/data with usrquota option, added persistent /etc/fstab entry
Set XFS user quota: bsoft=100m, bhard=100m for datauser on /srv/data
chown /srv/data to datauser:datauser
Verified enforcement: 80MB write succeeded, subsequent 40MB write correctly failed with EDQUOT once usage hit exactly 100MB (102400 blocks)
Cleaned up test files, confirmed quota usage reset to 0
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, mount state, quota report, fstab entry, datauser identity
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 (single node, non-concurrent)
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (646e5f74... -> e899d591...), proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart: verified /srv/data mount restored from fstab, quota configuration intact, datauser intact, and quota enforcement still functional (write over 100MB failed with Disk quota exceeded)

evidence.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB storage under /srv/data, enforced by filesystem
evidence.summary: xfs_quota report shows bsoft=bhard=102400 (100MB) for datauser on /srv/data; live test wrote exactly 100MB then dd failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' at the hard limit
Captured boot_id 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28, confirmed /srv/data mounted with usrquota, quota report healthy, fstab entry present, datauser exists
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded nohup so acknowledgement returned before disconnect; subsequent exec calls timed out/connection reset confirming node went down

evidence.requirement: changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: New boot_id e899d591-dfd4-48bf-b9d8-8a008c969a2e differs from baseline 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28, and uptime -s shows a later boot time

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of quota-enforced mount and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data mount restored automatically via fstab (usrquota option present), xfs_quota report shows correct 100MB limits still configured, datauser intact, and a live write test again correctly failed at exactly 100MB with 'Disk quota exceeded'
